variants.headline: Grant programme passes over needy districts
variants.sub: Districts in need were passed over by a government grant programme.
variants.body:
A government grant programme has passed over districts that needed it. The allocation is a public stewardship question, not an invitation to invent the recipients. Readers considering {target} should distinguish the established failure to reach need from an unreported claim about a motive, a sum or a private favour.

Our movement believes public provision should be judged by the purpose it is meant to serve. Need is not a decorative word for a programme's description. A political argument about grants should keep the overlooked districts at its centre rather than treating an allocation as virtuous simply because money was authorised.

We support {target} against a wider verdict built on assumption. The allocation defect deserves attention, but it does not prove every accusation about motives or justify an invented account of private favour. Political principle should remain visible when judgment becomes less comfortable.
